pois.name: Omo River
pois.city: Southern Nations, Nationalities, and Peoples' Region
pois.blurb: The Omo River (Amharic: ኦሞ ወንዝ, romanized: Omo Wenz; also called Omo-Bottego) in southern Ethiopia is the largest Ethiopian river outside the Nile Basin.

pois.name: Mount Wutai
pois.blurb: Mount Wutai, also known by its Chinese name Wutaishan and as Mount Qingliang, is a sacred Buddhist site at the headwaters of the Qingshui in Shanxi Province, China.

pois.name: Convent of the Barefoot Trinitarians
pois.blurb: The Convent of the Barefoot Trinitarians (Spanish: Convento de las Monjas Trinitarias Descalzas) is a convent located in Madrid, Spain.

pois.name: Keoladeo National Park
pois.blurb: Keoladeo National Park, or Keoladeo Ghana National Park, is a national park in Rajasthan, India.

pois.name: Museum Island
pois.blurb: The Museum Island (German: Museumsinsel, pronounced [muˈzeːʊmsˌɪnzl̩] ) is a museum complex on the northern part of Spree Island in the historic heart of Berlin, Germany.

pois.name: Rapa Nui National Park
pois.blurb: Rapa Nui National Park (Spanish: Parque nacional Rapa Nui) is a national park and UNESCO World Heritage Site located on Easter Island, Chile.

pois.name: World Heritage site No. 779
pois.blurb: The World Heritage Site (WHS) No. 779, Mount Emei Scenic Area, including Leshan Giant Buddha Scenic Area, includes: WHS No. 779-001: Mount Emei Scenic Area WHS No. 779-002: Leshan Giant Buddha Scenic Area,

pois.name: Caral
pois.blurb: The Sacred City of Caral-Supe, or simply Caral, is an archaeological site in Peru where the remains of the main city of the Caral civilization are found.

pois.name: Białowieża Forest
pois.blurb: Białowieża Forest is a large forest complex and World Heritage Area straddling the border between Poland and Belarus. It is one of the last and the largest remaining parts of the immense primeval forest that once stretched across the European Plain.

pois.name: Alt-Tempelhof (Berlin U-Bahn)
pois.blurb: Alt-Tempelhof (Old Tempelhof) is a Berlin U-Bahn station on the U6. It is located under Tempelhofer Damm in the centre of the former village of Tempelhof, now a Berlin district within the borough of Tempelhof-Schöneberg.

pois.name: Hendrik and Marri Oskam House
pois.blurb: The Hendrik and Marri Oskam House is a single-family residence located at 6901 Dakota Trail in Edina, Minnesota, United States.

pois.name: Olympic National Park
pois.blurb: Olympic National Park is a national park of the United States located in Washington, on the Olympic Peninsula. The park has four regions: the Pacific coastline, the west-side temperate rainforest, alpine areas, and the forests of the drier east side.

pois.name: Goguryeo tombs
pois.blurb: Goguryeo tombs, officially designated as the Complex of Koguryo Tombs (Korean: 고구려 고분군), are tombs in North Korea. In July 2004, they became the first UNESCO World Heritage site in the country.

pois.name: Kakadu National Park
pois.blurb: Kakadu National Park is a protected area in the Northern Territory of Australia, 171 km (106 mi) southeast of Darwin. It is a World Heritage Site.

pois.name: Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve
pois.blurb: The Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve is a protected area in the Gracias a Dios department region on the Caribbean coast of Honduras.

pois.name: Borobudur
pois.blurb: Borobudur, also transcribed Barabudur (Indonesian: Candi Borobudur, Javanese: ꦕꦤ꧀ꦝꦶꦧꦫꦧꦸꦝꦸꦂ, romanized: Candhi Barabudhur), is a 9th-century Mahayana Buddhist temple in Magelang Regency, near the town of Muntilan, northwest of the city of Yogyakarta, in Central Java, Indonesia.

pois.name: Palmyra
pois.blurb: Palmyra is an ancient city in central Syria. It is located in the eastern part of the Levant, and archaeological finds date back to the Neolithic period, and documents first mention the city in the early second millennium BCE.

pois.name: Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman
pois.blurb: The Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman are ancient water harvesting, transportation, storage and distribution systems from AD 500 located in the Omani regions of Dakhiliyah, Sharqiyah and Batinah.

pois.name: Medina of Marrakesh
pois.blurb: Marrakesh or Marrakech is the fourth-largest city in Morocco. It is one of the four imperial cities of Morocco and is the capital of the Marrakesh-Safi region.

pois.name: Skogskyrkogården
pois.blurb: Skogskyrkogården ([ˈskûːɡsɕʏrkʊˌɡoːɖɛn]; Swedish for 'The Woodland Cemetery') is a cemetery located in the Gamla Enskede district south of central Stockholm, Sweden.

pois.name: Church of Santa Engracia de Zaragoza
pois.wikipediaTitle: Church of Santa Engracia de Zaragoza
pois.blurb: The Church of Santa Engracia de Zaragoza is a basilica church in Zaragoza, Spain. It was built on the spot where Saint Engratia and her companions were said to have been martyred in 303 AD.

image.alt: Church of Santa Engracia de Zaragoza

pois.name: Sviyazhsk Assumption Monastery
pois.blurb: The Sviyazhsk Assumption Monastery (Russian: Свияжский Успенский монастырь) in Sviyazhsk, Republic of Tatarstan, Russia is a male Russian Orthodox monastery, included in UNESCO World Heritage list.

pois.name: Þingvellir
pois.blurb: Þingvellir (Icelandic: [ˈθiŋkˌvɛtlɪr̥] , anglicised as Thingvellir) was the site of the Alþing, the annual parliament of Iceland from the year 930 until the last session held at Þingvellir in 1798.

pois.name: Kaeng Krachan Forest Complex
pois.blurb: Kaeng Krachan Forest Complex (Thai: กลุ่มป่าแก่งกระจาน) is the inscribed name of a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Thailand.

pois.name: Bora Bora
pois.blurb: Bora Bora (French: Bora-Bora; Tahitian: Pora Pora) is a French island group in the Leeward Islands, comprising the western part of the Society Islands of French Polynesia, an overseas collectivity of the French Republic in the South Pacific.

clues.text: A place where inherited cultural meaning has outlasted changes in stewardship, use, or public role.
Its significance is tied to a built setting whose preservation matters as much as the activity once conducted there.
The site belongs to a Christian religious tradition and was altered during a later rebuilding campaign.
Its historical importance includes association with a major work of literature, not merely with worship or architecture.
A celebrated Spanish writer was buried there, though the burial record was disrupted when remains were moved during reconstruction.
Forensic investigators eventually identified the lost remains in 2015, confirming the burial connection after centuries of uncertainty.

reveal.title: Convent of the Barefoot Trinitarians
reveal.summary: The answer is the Convent of the Barefoot Trinitarians in Madrid, Spain. Miguel de Cervantes was buried there in 1616; his remains were moved during reconstruction in 1673, lost, and identified by forensic scientists in 2015.
reveal.clueExplanation: Clue 1 encoded the site's durable cultural meaning despite changing circumstances, reflected in its continuing association with Cervantes and its later investigation. Clue 2 pointed to a preserved built setting whose importance is inseparable from its former religious role. Clue 3 identified a Christian convent affected by reconstruction. Clue 4 shifted the focus from religious function to literary significance through the site's association with Cervantes. Clue 5 specified that a major Spanish writer was buried there and that reconstruction disrupted the burial record. Clue 6 supplied the confirmation: forensic scientists discovered and identified the remains in 2015 after they had been lost for centuries.
